'''Angkana Rüland''' (born 1987) is a German applied mathematician, a professor in mathematics and holder of a Hausdorff Chair in mathematics at the [[Hausdorff Center for Mathematics]] of the [[University of Bonn]]. Her research has included work on the mathematical modeling of [[shape-memory alloy]]s and on the [[inverse problem]]s arising in [[animal echolocation]].{{r|joins}}

==Education and career==
Rüland was born in 1987 in [[Chiang Mai]], but is a German citizen.{{r|diss}} She grew up in Bonn and was a mathematics student at the University of Bonn.{{r|joins}} She completed her doctorate in 2014 with the dissertation ''On Some Rigidity Properties in PDEs'' supervised by [[Herbert Koch]].{{r|mg|diss}}

After postdoctoral research at the [[University of Oxford]],{{r|joins}} working there with [[John M. Ball]],{{r|oxon}} she became a researcher at the [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics in the Sciences]] in 2017. She took a professorship at [[Heidelberg University]] in 2020 before returning to the University of Bonn in 2023.{{r|joins}}

==Recognition==
Rüland is one of the recipients of the 2024 [[New Horizons in Mathematics Prize]], associated with the [[Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics]], "for contributions to applied analysis, in particular the analysis of microstructure in solid-solid [[phase transition]]s and the theory of inverse problems".{{r|breakthrough}} In 2025, she received the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]].<ref name="j348">{{cite web | title=Prof. Dr. Angkana Rüland – Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz-Preisträgerin 2025 | website=DFG | url=https://www.dfg.de/de/gefoerderte-projekte/preistraeger-innen/leibniz-preis/2025/rueland | language=de | access-date=11 June 2025}}</ref>
